name: Josh Hawley

statements.quote: For my part, I have expressed my own sense of what our priorities ought to be when it comes to legislation. It’s very simple: workers, kids, consumers, and national security,
statements.venue: Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on principles for regulating AI (Hawley press release)

statements.quote: As Big Tech companies continue to develop new generations of artificial intelligence, the wide-ranging risks of their technology continue to grow unchecked and underreported. Simply stated, Congress must not allow our national security, civil liberties, and labor protections to take a back seat to AI. This bipartisan legislation would guarantee common-sense testing and oversight of the most advanced AI systems, so Congress and the American people can be better informed about potential risks.
statements.venue: Press release on AI Risk Evaluation Act, as reported by FedScoop

statements.quote: For too long, AI companies and Big Tech have deceived the public. They have stolen copyrighted work and hurt content creators and the average Joe across America while making themselves rich,
statements.venue: Statement to Axios ahead of Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on AI and copyright

statements.quote: For all of the talk about artificial intelligence and innovation, and the future that comes out of Silicon Valley, here's the truth that nobody wants to admit: AI companies are training their models on stolen material, period,
statements.venue: Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on AI training and copyrighted works

statements.quote: Congress needs to do something. I mean, if the answer is that the biggest corporation in the world, worth trillions of dollars, can come take an individual author’s work like Mr. Baldacci’s, lie about it, hide it, profit off of it, and there’s nothing our law does about that, we need to change the law.
statements.venue: Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on AI and copyright (Publishers Weekly)

statements.quote: AI chatbots pose a serious threat to our kids. More than seventy percent of American children are now using these AI products. Chatbots develop relationships with kids using fake empathy and are encouraging suicide. We in Congress have a moral duty to enact bright-line rules to prevent further harm from this new technology.
statements.venue: Statement to NBC News on GUARD Act

statements.quote: They are the richest companies in the history of the world, and they live by a motto that I think we’re all now all too familiar with, ‘move fast and break things.’ But increasingly, those things are our children,
statements.venue: Press conference introducing GUARD Act (Roll Call)

statements.quote: The new AI revolution that we have been promised will only be good for the American people if it actually protects America's children,
statements.venue: Press conference introducing GUARD Act (Punchbowl News)

statements.quote: Artificial intelligence is already replacing American workers, and experts project AI could drive unemployment up to 10-20% in the next five years,” said Senator Hawley. “The American people need to have an accurate understanding of how AI is affecting our workforce, so we can ensure that AI works for the people, not the other way around.
statements.venue: Press release on AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act

statements.quote: I want to protect kids from all those things, and I want the states to be able to do that.
statements.venue: Remarks on federal preemption of state AI laws (Governing)

statements.quote: The first thing we need to do is we need to pass legislation that would prevent AI chatbots from targeting minor children,
statements.venue: Axios onstage interview

statements.quote: People are not going to put up with that, and I think if you want to be pro-worker, you gotta start doing stuff for workers.
statements.venue: Axios onstage interview, on data centers and tech companies

statements.quote: We’re often told that this new dawning age of artificial intelligence is going to be a great age that will strengthen families and workers. I would just say that’s a choice, not an inevitability,
statements.venue: Senate Judiciary Committee markup of GUARD Act (Roll Call)

statements.quote: This should not happen in the United States of America. No amount of profit justifies the destruction of our families and our children.
statements.venue: Senate Judiciary Committee markup of GUARD Act (Medill News Service)

statements.quote: I mean, it is the worst kind of grooming. If that was a thing done by a human, the human would be in jail. We would call that sexual grooming.
statements.venue: Call with Fox News Digital on AI chatbots and GUARD Act

statements.quote: Silicon Valley’s proposed cure of a universal basic income gets the diagnosis backward. Work is about dignity, not just dollars. Pay a man to do nothing, and you have not solved his problem. You have deepened it.
statements.venue: Op-ed in The Free Press (AI and jobs)

statements.quote: The answer cannot be that the tech oligarchs reign supreme and the rest of us can just absorb their externalities. The companies building these facilities can afford to supply their own power, protect residential rates, and safeguard local water. We must hold them to that with binding legal requirements, not hollow promises.
statements.venue: Op-ed in The Free Press (data centers)

statements.quote: This is a form of corporate welfare. They don't need any welfare. These people are rich. They can pay their own way.
statements.venue: Fox News interview on data centers and opportunity zone tax breaks

statements.quote: As Chairman of the United States Senate Committee on Homeland Security’s Subcommittee on Disaster Management, I am investigating your AI agents’ hack of Hugging Face in July 2026 in light of new, disturbing evidence regarding the incident. My investigation will probe this AI hacking incident, along with growing allegations of the existential risk of new AI products.
statements.venue: Letter to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman

statements.quote: What happens to critical infrastructure, banks, and utilities if AI agents hack into their systems? How can personal data of millions of Americans be properly safeguarded? And who is held liable when AI goes rogue?
statements.venue: Letter to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman

statements.quote: What these companies need is not more power, to say nothing of a government handout, but some long-overdue accountability. One way to give it to them is to let the people they harm sue them in court.
statements.venue: Op-ed in The Washington Post

statements.quote: Whatever the truth of the doomsday scenarios, the latest AI products present real risks to real things Americans rely on — our financial system, hospitals, critical infrastructure. It’s no longer theoretical.
statements.venue: Op-ed in The Washington Post

statements.quote: I am introducing legislation in Congress to make the corporations liable for the actions of their agents when they design the agents in a reckless fashion. My legislation would also make users liable when they deploy the agents in a reckless way. And it would toughen criminal penalties.
statements.venue: Op-ed in The Washington Post (excerpt via Benton Institute)

statements.quote: AI-powered cameras produced by Flock and its competitors are tracking and creating digital footprints of everyday Americans — a nightmare for individual liberties unless Congress enacts meaningful rules and accountability,
statements.venue: Statement to CBS News on STOP Flock Abuse Act

statements.quote: We are watching a handful of companies assemble a concentration of capital, information, and political power without precedent in the American experience.
statements.venue: Quoted in Brookings analysis

raw:
I found 21 statements by Sen. Hawley on AI. They cover chatbots and kids, AI liability and rogue agents, copyright, jobs, data centers, AI-powered surveillance, state preemption and the legislative priorities he named at a 2023 hearing. All quotes come from search-result text.

- **Dates:** The Hawley, Blumenthal and Amodei hearing is dated 2023-07 from my own recollection. The search result gave 2024-07-08, which looks unreliable. The Brookings quote has no date in the source, so I gave it none.
- **Sources:** I took several quotes from news outlets rather than Hawley's own site, because those pages showed the full text.
- **Left out:** I skipped fragments that were too short or altered by brackets. I also skipped one pull-quote about Google and classrooms because the page didn't clearly attribute it to Hawley.
